newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ANZ says Tel Aviv branch "inevitable".
newsitem.headline: ANZ says Tel Aviv branch "inevitable".

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group said on Thursday, a day after opening a branch in Arab East Jerusalem, that an ANZ branch in Tel Aviv was inevitable.

Branch Manager Ian Rutherford, asked to comment on media reports that ANZ would also open a branch in Tel Aviv, told Reuters: "The answer to that is I think that is premature." But he added such a move was "both desirable and inevitable".
Israel's central bank, which licensed the Jerusalem branch, said on Thursday it hoped the bank would help strengthen ties between Israeli and Asian investors.
ANZ chairman Don Mercer came to Jerusalem for the opening, meeting Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel.

"In the meeting the governor and the chairman of the Australian bank examined the possibility that Israel would become the financial centre of the Middle East," the Bank of Israel said in a statement.
ANZ is the only overseas bank to have a commercial banking licence from Israeli authorities.
The branch was officially opened at a time of high tensions between Israel and Palestinians over Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

Under interim peace deals signed with Israel since 1993, Palestinians have no official say in matters relating to Jerusalem, whose future is to be decided in talks on a permanent peace accord. But they demand Israel take no unilateral action to prejudice the outcome of those negotiations.
